alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes the connective (rule 14).
Finite verb takes its subject pronoun (rule 17); head on the lexical verb.
Pronominal suffix takes the object pronoun (rule 18).
The fronted question auxiliary belongs to the interrogative particle (rule 17).
The verb keeps its subject pronoun and lexical verb (rule 17).
Vocative noun; no supplied 'O' or 'ye' is written here (rule 36).
No object morpheme stands with 'seen'; a supplied object pronoun answers to nothing and does not join the verb (rule 44).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).

Causative rendered by a second verb; head on the complement verb (rule 44). Unit discontinuous around the object pronoun (rule 25). Corrected: the following 'to' is not part of this rendering, since the verb's object is the suffix and שְׂפַת הַנָּחַל is a directional accusative, so rule 44's bare-object clause does not reach it.

Goal accusative with no preposition on it: the supplied 'to' is licensed by the noun's own case-function and stands before the phrase it opens, exactly as rule 33's 'to your mountain', while the supplied 'the' goes on the construct and the rectum's article takes the written one (rule 29). The competing reading gives 'to' to the causative verb under rule 44, but that clause governs a bare direct object, and this verb's object is the suffix.
The rectum's article takes the 'the' standing before its own word (rule 29).

review_notes: Corrected: the 'to' of 'to the bank of the river' moves from the causative verb to the noun. Rule 44's supplied-preposition clause requires a bare direct object, but הֵשִׁיב's object is the suffix 'me'; שְׂפַת הַנָּחַל is a directional accusative, which is rule 33's own example ('to your mountain').
'this' after 'hast thou seen' remains added: no object morpheme stands in the clause (rule 44).
The vocative בֶן־אָדָם takes no supplied 'O' here, and its 'of' belongs to the rectum (rules 19, 36).
